body: HOW TO USE: every flag that fires on a candidate gets one row, written down before a decision, and saved as a decision/analysis record (L10). Hard disqualifiers (fraud signals, auditor exit citing information denial, related-party diversion, fake-cash signals) are NOT overridable by this template. ROW FORMAT: FLAG (metric, value, years) | CONTEXT QUESTIONS | EVIDENCE THAT CLEARS (must come from outside the company's own P&L where possible) | EVIDENCE THAT CONFIRMS | VERDICT (cleared / open / confirmed) | WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY MIND | REVIEW DATE. EXAMPLES: High P/E -> Is EPS depressed? Reverse DCF implied growth vs reinvestment x ROIC? P/E vs own median? -> clears: implied growth below demonstrated, unit data shows runway; confirms: P/E >2x own median, slowing unit growth. Negative FCF/low CFO -> What asset is being built? Whose working capital? -> clears: own inventory/sovereign debtor/high-ROCE capex; confirms: receivables to related or unknown parties, WC sign contradicts model. Rising debt -> Lease, GML, govt dues or bank/CP? Tenor? -> clears: lease/GML/long-tenor; confirms: short funds long, debt + negative CFO. Pledge -> six checks (insight:flag-pledge-severity). High ROE/ROCE -> DuPont; CFO/PAT; peer gap; lender growth vs system. Cash pile -> yield, location, cash+debt. Receivables -> counterparty, ageing, related-party share. Losses/dilution -> unit economics; price x purpose x buyer; per-share outcome. Low margin -> ROCE and WC days. RULES: a flag cleared only by management's explanation stays OPEN; if 3+ flags stay open, no position without a variant view; record false alarms and missed traps afterwards to calibrate the checklist.

data.rule: management explanation alone = open; 3+ open = no position without variant view

title: Flag override template: flag -> context questions -> evidence that clears -> evidence that confirms

body: Same-method promise scores for four Indian IT mid-caps (last 6 calls each, Jul-2025 to Nov-2026; Persistent held no Q1FY27 call, its Jun-2026 Nagarro call is used). Weighted delivery (credit, specificity-weighted): PERSISTENT 100.0% (n=4), COFORGE 85.0% (n=10), MPHASIS 58.3% (n=8), KPITTECH 95.5% (n=5). Sector pattern: near-term company-level margin guidance (EBIT/EBITDA bands, quarter-ahead margin walks) is almost always met (pooled margin 97.5%); growth-shape, vertical and timing statements are the weak part (pooled revenue/growth 68.8%, other 82.4%). Most FY27 guidance is still pending and n is small (4-10 scored per company), so the big tests - KPIT's FY27 20.5-21.2% EBITDA guide against a 17.2-17.8% H1, Persistent's USD 2 bn and 16-17% EBIT aspirations, Coforge's raised 16% EBIT, Mphasis's low-double-digit growth - are not yet in the scores. SAC (pts vs leave-one-out peer medians): PERSISTENT +13.9, COFORGE +12.6, MPHASIS -28.5, KPITTECH +6.6. Use: base rates for credibility-generated paper calls (thesis tag credibility-generated, it). Provisional. Research, not advice.

data.adjustment_rule: p0 = leave-one-out pooled STRICT delivery rate (specificity-weighted share 'delivered'; partly=0) of the other 3 peers in the promise's category (all-category peer rate if <8 peer promises in that category). p = clip(p0 + N/(N+20) x SAC/100, 0.05, 0.95), N = company's scored promises, SAC in points (credit basis: delivered 1, partly 0.5; categories with n<5, or with <2 peers having data, pooled). P(base) = p0.

title: Base rate for management promise delivery in Indian IT mid-caps (PERSISTENT, COFORGE, MPHASIS, KPITTECH; Nov 2026)
